In this era's diet, the poor ate barley, oats and rye while pricier wheat went to the better-off — all consumed as bread, porridge, gruel and pasta, since rice arrived late and the potato wasn't yet around. What food tradition is this?
Colonial history of the United States
Medieval cuisine: Foods, eating habits, and cooking methods of the Middle Ages.
A rear admiral in the Austro-Hungarian Navy who fought at the Strait of Otranto, this man went on to rule his landlocked nation as regent from 1920 through most of World War II. Who was he?
Miklós Horthy: Regent of Hungary from 1920 to 1944.
Meaning 'seal' or 'gesture' in Sanskrit, this hand or body pose is used in Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist ritual as well as yoga and Indian dance — what is it called?
Mudra: Symbolic gestures in Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism.
Serving as Chief Minister of Odisha for 24 years until 2024, this politician also founded the Biju Janata Dal in 1997 — who is he?
Trained as a classical ballet instructor and educated in Czechoslovakia, this monarch ascended the Cambodian throne in 2004, just a week after his father's abdication — who is he?
Norodom Sihamoni: King of Cambodia since 2004.
Nicknamed 'the Young,' this Ottoman sultan came to the throne in 1618 and was killed in a regicide just four years later — who was he?
Osman II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1618 to 1622.
This British Conservative served as Leader of the House of Commons from 2022 to 2024, ran for party leadership against Liz Truss, and later lost her Portsmouth North seat in 2024 — who is she?
In 1996, a gunman killed 35 people at a historic Tasmanian tourist site, leading to sweeping changes in Australia's gun laws — what is this tragedy called?
Port Arthur massacre: 1996 mass shooting in Tasmania, Australia.
Serving as Ecuador's president from 2007 to 2017, this democratic socialist economist has lived in Belgium since leaving office — who is he?
Rafael Correa: President of Ecuador from 2007 to 2017. Correa won the presidency in the 2006 general election on a platform criticizing the established political elites.
Which Titan tricked her husband into swallowing a rock instead of their infant son, having already borne five other future Olympian gods?
Rhea (mythology): Ancient Greek goddess and mother of the gods.
A British peeress and former model who once worked as a political staffer, she is married to the 7th Marquess of Cholmondeley — who is she?
Grand Duchess Tatiana Nikolaevna of Russia
Rose Hanbury: English peeress and model (born 1984)

After publicizing the Gold Rush and founding San Francisco's first newspaper, this Latter-day Saint became California's first millionaire — before his vigilance-committee actions got him disfellowshipped — who was he?

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Lasting 872 days and killing an estimated 1.5 million from a prewar population of 3.2 million, this WWII blockade of the Soviet Union's second-largest city was never successfully captured — what was it?
Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.
Dubbed the "King of Gambling," this billionaire held a 40-year government monopoly over Macau's casinos and split his fortune among children who run MGM Macau and City of Dreams — who was he?

Founder of a political party built around reforming Japan's public broadcaster, this activist-turned-politician won a House of Councillors seat in 2019 before forfeiting it to run in a by-election — who is he?
Born into Virginia's planter class, he served as second vice president before becoming the third U.S. president — and famously penned the Declaration of Independence — who was he?
Thomas Jefferson: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1801 to 1809.
This boy pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty undid his predecessor's experiment with worshipping a single sun-disk god and restored Egypt's traditional pantheon — who is he?
Tutankhamun: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1333 to 1324 BC.
Named for a queen who reigned from 1837 until 1901, this period saw the Irish Famine and the Crimean War against Russia — what was it called?
Victorian era: Queen Victoria's reign, 1837 to 1901.

In 1806, fearing Napoleon's growing power after the Confederation of the Rhine formed, Prussia joined Russia, Saxony, Sweden and Britain in a fresh multinational stand against the French Empire — which conflict?
War of the Fourth Coalition: 1806–1807 conflict of the Napoleonic Wars.
It's the season that arrives when your hemisphere tilts away from the Sun, so that while one half of Earth shivers the other basks in summer. Which season?
Winter: Coldest of the four temperate seasons.
He ran the KGB for 15 years before briefly becoming the Soviet Union's General Secretary in 1982 — and decades earlier, as ambassador to Hungary, helped crush its 1956 uprising. Who is he?
Yuri Andropov: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1982 to 1984.
Which one below was born first?
Mikhail Lomonosov (born 1711) is the earliest of the four. One of the founders of modern geology, Lomonosov was also a poet and influenced the formation of the modern Russian literary language.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four. It was originally developed at Massachusetts General Hospital for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Maria Mitchell is an astronomer. Maria Mitchell ( mə-RY-ə; August 1, 1818 – June 28, 1889) was an American astronomer, librarian, naturalist, and educator.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Barium?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
What is the atomic number of Nickel?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
In what year was Zhuge Liang born?
Zhuge Liang: After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
In what year was John McAfee born?
John McAfee: In 1987, he wrote the first commercial anti-virus software, founding McAfee Associates to sell his creation.
In what year was Max Planck born?
Max Planck: Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck (German: [ˈmaks ˈplaŋk]; 23 April 1858 – 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
In what year did Vikram Sarabhai die?
Vikram Sarabhai: Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
In what year did Michael Faraday die?
Michael Faraday: Although Faraday received little formal education, as a self-made man, he was one of the most influential scientists in history.
In what year was Lithium discovered?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Which country is Dassault Falcon 900 from?
Dassault Falcon 900: France. The Dassault Falcon 900, commonly abbreviated as the F900, is a French-built corporate trijet aircraft made by Dassault Aviation.
Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this economist ran the Federal Reserve for its second-longest tenure ever — who is he?
Alan Greenspan (born March 6, 1926) is an American economist who served as the 13th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006.
Before sharing the 2010 Nobel for graphene, this Manchester physicist won an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog using its own magnetism — who is he?
Andre Geim (born 21 October 1958) is a Russian-born British physicist working in England in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester.

Which plant family of about 181 genera and 2,600 species, nearly all found in the tropics, includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms with large fan- or feather-shaped fronds atop mostly unbranched stems?
Arecaceae are a family of perennial, flowering plants in the monocot order Arecales.
Native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins, this freshwater catfish is marketed in the US as "swai" and in the UK as "river cobbler" — which fish?

Basa (fish) (Pangasius bocourti), as it is commonly referred to, is a species of primarily freshwater-dwelling catfish in the shark-catfish family, Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins of Mainland Southeast Asia.
Caused by a recessive allele in the leopard but a dominant one in the jaguar, this dark melanistic variant still secretly carries its usual rosettes — what is it called?
Black panther is the melanistic colour variant of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar (Panthera onca).

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Made of one oxygen atom triple-bonded to a single atom of the element that also forms diamonds and graphite, this colorless, odorless, poisonous gas is slightly less dense than air and typically arises from incomplete combustion — name the compound?
Carbon monoxide (chemical formula CO) is a poisonous, flammable gas that is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and slightly less dense than air.

Native to North America except for one species found mostly in Asia, these small striped rodents are technically classified as squirrels and pack food into cheek pouches for winter storage — what are they?
Chipmunk are small, striped squirrels of subtribe Tamiina.

Making up 25 to 35 percent of protein content in mammals, this triple-helix structural protein is the main component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage, bone, tendons, and skin — name the protein?
Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.

The first anatomically modern humans known to inhabit Europe and Siberia, arriving as early as 56,800 years ago, this population interbred with the indigenous Neanderthals before the latter went extinct — who are they?
Cro-Magnon (EEMH) were the first early modern humans (Homo sapiens) found in Europe and Siberia, continuously occupying the continent possibly from as early as 56,800 years ago.
This biological process breaks down large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components for absorption into the bloodstream, via both mechanical and chemical means. What is it?
Digestion is the breakdown of large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components so that they can be absorbed into the blood plasma.

This order of about 1,000 predatory fish species undergoes dramatic transformation from a distinctive larval stage to its adult form, and includes roughly 20 different families — what are these long, snake-like fish called?
Eel are ray-finned fish belonging to the order Anguilliformes, which consists of eight suborders, 20 families, 164 genera, and about 1000 species.
Also called grain alcohol, this volatile compound with the formula C2H5OH is the active ingredient in every alcoholic beverage — what is it?
Ethanol (also called ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol, or simply alcohol) is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH.
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Flamingo are a type of wading bird in the family Phoenicopteridae, which is the only extant family in the order Phoenicopteriformes.
Its name literally means 'Earth writing,' and it explores not just where things are but how they changed and came to be across the planet — what field is it?
Geography (from Ancient Greek geographia; combining ge 'Earth' and graphein 'write', lit. 'Earth writing') is the study of the lands, features, inhabitants, and phenomena of planet Earth.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow in mathematics, this American's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual solution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who is she?

Julia Robinson (December 8, 1919 - July 30, 1985) was an American mathematician noted for her contributions to the fields of computability theory and computational complexity theory - most notably in decision problems.
Which aromatic Mediterranean evergreen tree, prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture and used to season food, can grow up to 20 meters tall with smooth, glossy leaves?
Laurus nobilis is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves.
Because its large profile and low operating altitude make it an easy target, this heavily armed gunship variant of the C-130 Hercules usually flies missions at night. What aircraft is it?
Lockheed AC-130 is a heavily armed, long-endurance, ground-attack variant of the C-130 Hercules transport, fixed-wing aircraft.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this west-central African monkey wears red and blue on both its face and its rump, with the brightest males being the biggest — long mistaken for a baboon, what is it?
Mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx) is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa.
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
First synthesized in 2003 by Russian and American scientists at Dubna, this synthetic element — atomic number 115 — was named in 2016 for the oblast around its birthplace — what is it?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Found across North America, Europe, North Africa, and Asia, this three-stage amphibian passes through an aquatic larval phase and a land-dwelling 'eft' stage before adulthood — what is it?
Newt is a salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Its name means 'serpent-bearer' in Ancient Greek — this large constellation straddling the celestial equator is depicted as a man grasping a snake — name it?
Ophiuchus (o-fee-) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
A physician in this medical field — devoted to the study of disease and diagnosing it largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — is called a pathologist. What is the field?
Pathology is the study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.
Named from the Greek for an infinite carbon chain it would ultimately become, this class of organic compounds strings together alternating single and triple bonds. What is it called?
Polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds; that is, a series of consecutive alkynes, (CC)n with n greater than 1.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This inflammatory disease typically develops two to four weeks after a streptococcal throat infection and can damage the heart valves in about half of cases — what is it?
Rheumatic fever (RF) is an inflammatory disease that can involve the heart, joints, skin, and brain.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
These eight-legged arachnids inject venom through their fangs and extrude silk from spinnerets, ranking as the largest order in their class — what are they?
Spider (order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods that have eight limbs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk.
A starchy tuber from the morning-glory family, often confused with yams in North America despite being only distantly related to them — what root vegetable is it?
Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a dicotyledonous plant in the morning glory family, Convolvulaceae.
This part of the lower limb sits between the hip and the knee, containing a single thick bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below — name the body part?
Thigh is the area between the hip (pelvis) and the knee.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

This English fashion designer, largely responsible for bringing punk fashion into the mainstream, ran a boutique on King's Road with her partner, whose band helped define the 1970s UK punk scene — who is she?

Vivienne Westwood (ne Swire; 8 April 1941 - 29 December 2022) was an English fashion designer and businesswoman, largely responsible for bringing modern punk and new wave fashions into the mainstream.
This Russian political activist and economist, described as the 'first lady' of her country's opposition, vowed to continue her late husband's work after fleeing into exile. Who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya (ne Abrosimova; born 24 July 1976) is a Russian political activist and economist.

A key figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, this philosopher wrote The Theory of Moral Sentiments before the 1776 work often called the inception of modern economics — who is the "father of economics"?
Adam Smith: Scottish economist and philosopher (1723–1790)
Belonging to the birch family and found throughout the north temperate zone, this genus of about 35 tree and shrub species even reaches into the Andes — what genus is it?
Alder: Genus of flowering plants in the birch family Betulaceae.
Sold under the brand name Norvasc, this long-acting calcium channel blocker treats high blood pressure and variant angina by relaxing and widening the arteries — what's the drug?
Amlodipine: Medication against high blood pressure.
Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões, this 13th-century Portuguese Catholic priest joined the Order of Friars Minor — who is he?
Anthony of Padua: Portuguese Catholic saint (1195–1231)
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Sold under the brand name Tessalon, this cough-relief medication works within about 20 minutes by acting as a local anesthetic that blocks stretch receptors in the lungs — what is this drug called?
Benzonatate: Oral cough medication. Benzonatate, sold under the brand name Tessalon among others, is a medication that is used for the symptomatic relief of cough.

Native to North America and classified in the genus Vaccinium, this fruit comes in wild 'lowbush' and cultivated 'highbush' varieties, with Canada leading global production of the wild type — what fruit is it?
Blueberry: Perennial plant with blue berries.
This rhythmic process of inhaling and exhaling delivers oxygen to the alveoli and removes carbon dioxide, with its per-minute rate counted as a vital sign — what is it?
Breathing: Process of moving air in and out of the lungs.
With the formula CaC2, this industrial compound reacts with trace moisture to give off a garlicky smell and is used to generate acetylene gas in old-fashioned lamps — what is it?
Calcium carbide: Chemical compound. Its main use industrially is in the production of acetylene and calcium cyanamide.
This mammalian order of flesh-eating species is split into cat-like and dog-like suborders, Feliformia and Caniformia, and ranks as the sixth-largest order of mammals — which order?
Carnivora: Order of mammals. Carnivora ( kar-NIV-ər-ə) is an order of placental mammals specialised primarily in eating flesh, whose members are formally referred to as carnivorans.
Known in North America as fireweed and in Britain as rosebay willowherb, this perennial flowering plant thrives across the boreal forests of the Northern Hemisphere — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium: Species of flowering plant in the willowherb family.
This fluoroquinolone antibiotic treats everything from typhoid fever to urinary tract infections but can rarely cause tendon rupture — what drug?
Ciprofloxacin: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.
This medical term describes inflammation of the large intestine, used both when the cause is undiagnosed and for its specific ulcerative form — what condition is it?
Colitis: Inflammation of the colon (large intestine). Colitis may be acute and self-limited or long-term.
This mostly inactive steroid hormone is created when an enzyme shields organs like the kidneys by converting active cortisol into its inactive form — what is it?
Cortisone: Corticosteroid precursor and metabolite of cortisol.
Started in 1955 by an army colonel and a cynologist as an experiment, this hybrid dog breed became officially recognized as a national breed in 1982 — which one?
Czechoslovakian Wolfdog: Czech and Slovak breed of dog.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
This Eastern Han hydrologist is credited as the first to harness a waterwheel to power the bellows of a blast furnace for forging cast iron — who was this ingenious engineer?
Du Shi: 1st-century engineer, metallurgist and politician.
This Hungarian nuclear chemist became the world's leading expert in isotope separation and polonium preparation, and confirmed the existence of "Uranium-Y" — who was she?
This class of chemical compound forms when an acid's hydroxyl hydrogen is swapped for an organic group, and includes the glycerides that make up most animal fats — what is it?
Ester: Compound derived from an acid.
First confirmedly detected in 1992 orbiting a pulsar, this term describes any planet found outside our solar system — what is it?
Exoplanet: Planet outside of the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.
From the Latin word for 'tube' or 'pipe,' this medical term describes an abnormal connection between two hollow spaces in the body — what is it?
Fistula: Abnormal connection between two hollow bodily spaces, often organs.
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.

The largest species of its kind in the world, this circumglobal sea creature was reclassified in 2017 after DNA testing showed it was more closely related to a different genus than to its smaller reef-dwelling cousin — what is it?
Giant oceanic manta ray: Species of cartilaginous fish.
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?

Recognizable by V-shaped nostrils and a layer of blubber that keeps it warm in Arctic and temperate coastal waters, this pinniped is the most widely distributed of its kind and can weigh up to 370 pounds — which species?
Harbor seal: Species of pinniped. Blubber under the seal's skin helps to maintain body temperature.
This seasonal state of drastically reduced metabolism, breathing, and heart rate lets animals conserve energy through winter months, with 'aestivation' as its summer counterpart — what is it called?
Hibernation: Physiological state of dormant inactivity in order to pass the winter season.
This poisonous gas or liquid with the formula HF dissolves in water to form a corrosive acid and serves as the chief industrial source of fluorine — what is it?
Native to the subcontinent, the male of this bird species is called a peacock and sports a fan-shaped crest with a dazzling train of eyespot feathers used in courtship — which species?
Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.
Awarded a gas-attack Iron Cross in WWI before sharing the 1925 Nobel with Gustav Hertz for the laws of how an electron strikes an atom — who was this German-American physicist?
This Hungarian-American polymath helped build the mathematical framework of quantum physics and codified ideas from game theory to cellular automata — who was he?
John von Neumann: Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957)
A biologist and botanist married four times — her last husband directed the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos lab — she was played by Emily Blunt in a 2023 film. Who was she?
This small Arctic rodent is the unwitting star of a persistent myth that it hurls itself off cliffs in mass suicide — what is it?
Lemming: Tribe of rodents of the family Cricetidae.

A domesticated South American camelid whose Quechua name the Spanish adopted, this herd animal can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles and learns simple tasks after a few tries — what is it?
Llama: Species of wooly domesticated mammal.
Popular as companion birds despite conservation concerns for several species, these large, long-tailed, brightly colored New World parrots belong to the tribe Arini — what are they?
Macaw: Group of birds in the parrot family.
On April 3, 1973, this Motorola engineer made history's first public call from a handheld cell phone on a Manhattan sidewalk — who is he?
Cataloged as a nebula by a French astronomer in 1781, this supergiant elliptical galaxy boasts roughly 15,000 globular clusters, a hundred times more than our own — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87: Galaxy in the constellation Virgo.
Nicknamed the 'sensitive plant,' this legume's leaves fold inward within seconds of being touched and reopen a few minutes later — what plant is it?
Mimosa pudica: Species of creeping annual plant.
Serving King Roger II in Norman Sicily, this Arab geographer created the Tabula Rogeriana, one of the most advanced world maps of the medieval era — who was he?
Known in Sanskrit as Padma or Kamala, this aquatic plant is often called sacred lotus though true water lilies actually belong to a different family — what species?
Nelumbo nucifera: Species of aquatic flowering plant. It is sometimes colloquially called a water lily, though this more often refers to members of the family Nymphaeaceae.
Named for the daring Doolittle airmen of World War II, this subsonic stealth flying wing is being built to replace the B-1 and B-2 by 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: American stealth bomber aircraft.

This dental specialty treats misaligned teeth and jaws, a condition worldwide diets of softer foods have made even more common by leaving smaller jaws with less room to fit them. What specialty is it?
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Featuring an R−O−O−R backbone where two oxygen atoms bond directly to each other, what name covers this class of molecules?
Peroxide: Chemical compounds with the structure R–O–O–R'
Manufactured in Switzerland since 1991, this pressurized single-engine turboprop's large aft cargo door has made it popular with air-ambulance operators and police departments alike — which aircraft?
Pilatus PC-12: Swiss executive and utility transport aircraft.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Also called false saffron, this thistle-like annual is one of the world's oldest crops, prized today for the vegetable oil pressed from its seeds — what plant is it?
Safflower: Species of plant. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
